title: Pelion Dynamics QBR — Usage, Cost & Reliability Roadmap
summary: Quarterly health review covering token usage growth, two unexpected cost spikes tied to a model rollout, latency incidents during peak windows, and alignment on the next three-month roadmap including pilot for Dedicated capacity and a private VPC trial. Agreed to run a focused cost-for-latency tradeoff experiment and share a detailed pricing scenario. Action owners assigned for benchmark run, security docs, and pilot kickoff.
topics: Roadmap: Dedicated pilot, VPC onboarding, cache/batching improvements
Next steps: benchmarks, pricing scenarios, security review
action_items: Liam Ortiz: run 72-hour latency + throughput benchmark for prod traffic patterns (due 2026-05-20)
Jess Torres: share internal incident timeline and K8s pod metrics for 2026-04-28 outage (due 2026-05-17)
Maya Chen: send tailored Dedicated pricing scenarios and pilot SOW draft (due 2026-05-15)
Aria Gupta: schedule security docs walkthrough and provide SOC2/HSM integration notes (due 2026-05-18)
next_steps: Redwood to deliver cost vs latency tradeoff deck and two pricing scenarios
Run benchmark (Redwood SE) against Pelion traffic in staging
Customer to confirm pilot users + acceptance criteria
Security review meeting to be scheduled w/ Pelion security team
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE); Aria Gupta (Redwood CSM); Nora Patel (Pelion Head of ML); Samir Venkatesh (Pelion VP Eng); Jess Torres (Pelion SRE); Diego Marquez (Pelion Product)
Deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/pelion-qbr-2026.pdf
Benchmarks: https://redwood.example.com/bench/pelion-2026-staging.xlsx

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time for the QBR. we want to go through usage, the two cost blips you saw in april, reliability incidents, and the roadmap/next steps. quick intros?
[00:18] Nora Patel: Nora here - head of ML at Pelion. thanks for coordinating. we'll be focused on, um, the forecasting and the dedicated pilot ask.
[00:26] Samir Venkatesh: Samir - VP Eng. I'll be listening for capacity implications and cost commitments.
[00:32] Maya Chen: great. Liam, do you want to kick off with the usage trend slide?
[00:36] Liam Ortiz: yeah sure. so slide 4 shows token growth - month over month up about 38% in the last quarter, driven by increased batch inferencing from the recommendations product. there's a tail of long sequences - average seq len went from 420 to around 560 which increases token cost and KV cache pressure.
[01:05] Nora Patel: can i interrupt — that sequence jump coincides with the new product flow we shipped on april 12, it's longer context windows for the multimodal pipeline.
[01:13] Liam Ortiz: yep that matches. also worth noting batching improved throughput but at peak it raised 95th percentile latency because the batcher held requests slightly longer to reach target batch sizes. tradeoff.
[01:29] Jess Torres: to add we saw two notable cost spikes - april 14 and april 29. the first aligned with the rollout, the second looked like a retry storm when an internal cache warmed incorrectly.
[01:41] Maya Chen: thanks Jess, that's useful. Aria, do you want to summarize the billing report we sent?
[01:46] Aria Gupta: sure - we parsed April's invoice and isolated the anomalies: the april 14 event is primarily model variant m-7b-highmem usage; april 29 is an orchestration-level retry and burst due to a misconfigured backoff. together they accounted for ~17% of monthly spend. baseline growth is about 9% excluding incidents.
[02:08] Diego Marquez: question — does the baseline include the cache miss rate? we haven't fully instrumented that on our side.
[02:14] Liam Ortiz: our telemetry shows cache hits dropped during rollout windows because model rollout invalidated prefixes; we saw an increased KV miss by roughly 22% during those windows.
[02:24] Samir Venkatesh: so the cost increase is a combo of longer sequences, batch hold, and cache miss — seems multi-factor.
[02:30] Maya Chen: exactly. let's move to the reliability incidents timeline — Jess can you walk us through the April 29 incident?
[02:36] Jess Torres: yeah. so at 03:12 UTC our orchestrator retried a subset of requests after a transient DB timeout; retries caused a cascade to the inference pool; autoscaler pulled extra nodes but those nodes hit cold-start for large models and increased p99 latency for about 18 minutes. we closed the incident at 03:30 after adding short-circuit logic.
[03:03] Nora Patel: do you have the pod-level logs? we can correlate with our deploy hooks.
[03:06] Jess Torres: i'll drop a slice of logs to the channel after — i have them.
[03:10] Liam Ortiz: quick note — cold-start behavior for large models is something Redwood can help mitigate via warm pools or pinned instances in Dedicated. that was one of the reasons Pelion asked about Dedicated.
[03:24] Samir Venkatesh: yes, the business is sensitive to those 15–20 minute blips. what's the expected latency SLO with Dedicated?
[03:32] Maya Chen: with Dedicated you can get much tighter p99 targets — typical configs we've seen keep p99 under 500–700ms for these model sizes depending on sequence length and batching policy. we'll include exact numbers in the pricing scenarios.
[03:46] Diego Marquez: what about private VPC? data residency and audit trails are blockers for our security team.
[03:52] Aria Gupta: we support Private deployments with customer-managed networking; we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and provide audit logs and longer retention for traces. we have a SOC2 package and an HSM integration guide we'll share.
[04:08] Nora Patel: moving on to roadmap — Pelion wants two pilots: a Dedicated reserved pool for the top 10% of traffic and a VPC-onboarding trial for compliance-sensitive flows. acceptance is: no more than 2% latency regressions and cost neutral vs current baseline over 30 days, excluding incidents.
[04:28] Maya Chen: good explicit criteria. Liam, what test would you run to validate cost neutrality?
[04:32] Liam Ortiz: we'll run a 72-hour staging replay with Pelion traffic that mirrors seq length distribution and arrival patterns. measure tokens, batching efficiency, and KV hit rates, then run the same traffic across Hosted and a Dedicated config to compare unit economics.
[04:48] Samir Venkatesh: timeline? we need results before our June exec review.
[04:52] Maya Chen: we can plan benchmark next week and deliver findings by May 20. action assigned to Liam.
[04:58] Diego Marquez: security review — our secops needs details on key rotation, audit logs frequency and where logs are stored.
[05:04] Aria Gupta: we'll send the security pack; if needed we can set a separate meeting with your secops for deep dive.
[05:12] Jess Torres: one more ops ask: automatic fallback policies — we need guaranteed automatic fallback to a smaller model variant under overload without causing cascading retries.
[05:22] Liam Ortiz: we have routing policies that can fall back to compatible variants and automatic throttles to prevent retry storms. we should prototype fallback threshold settings in the benchmark.
[05:33] Nora Patel: also, can we get guidance on quantization? we saw quality dip when our team tried int8 on the 7b — we need a quantization recommendation for our RLHF-augmented models.
[05:45] Liam Ortiz: absolutely. Redwood Optimize has model-specific quantization guidance and we can run a quick eval on a held-out prompt set to quantify quality delta.
[05:56] Maya Chen: ok, let's capture open items: benchmarks, security docs, pilot SOW, incident logs. Aria will schedule secops call.
[06:05] Diego Marquez: quick pricing question — if we reserve Dedicated capacity for 12 months what's the typical uplift?
[06:10] Maya Chen: depends on commit size and burst allowances; we'll include two scenarios: 6-month pilot with month-to-month billing and 12-month reserved with a discount and capacity guarantees. you'll see token/unit price delta in the deck.
[06:26] Samir Venkatesh: will we be able to split traffic by route to Dedicated vs Hosted? we don't want to route everything.
[06:33] Liam Ortiz: yes routing policies support per-route pinning; also automated fallback to Hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[06:40] Nora Patel: question about observability retention — we need at least 90 days of token-level billing and trace retention for audits.
[06:47] Aria Gupta: we can provide that as an add-on; we'll include retention options and costs in the proposal.
[06:55] Jess Torres: small nit — can you log correlation ids in a way that maps to our internal request ids? that will make post-incident forensics easier.
[07:01] Liam Ortiz: yes we support pluggable request id mapping. we'll show config snippets in the follow up.
[07:08] Maya Chen: closing the loop — recap of next steps: Redwood to run benchmarks and share deck by May 20, Redwood to send Dedicated pricing scenarios and SOW by May 15, Pelion to share incident logs and define pilot users by May 17, security deep dive to be scheduled (Aria).
[07:28] Nora Patel: sounds good, appreciate the actionability. one ask — include a lightweight A/B test design in your benchmark so we can validate quality vs quantized models.
[07:38] Liam Ortiz: will do, we'll include a holdout set and automatic eval hooks.
[07:42] Diego Marquez: ok thanks — we'll await the artifacts.
[07:46] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and dates.
[07:50] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some words auto-corrected (e.g., kv cache referred to as "K V cache" in transcript), occasional speaker mislabels early in the call but validated against attendee list.
notes: Reference artifacts shared: QBR deck, benchmark sheet. Pelion requested SOC2 and HSM details. Agreed on acceptance criteria and timelines for pilot. Next exchange will be focused benchmark results and pricing scenarios.
